proposals.evidence: Platts explicitly records de-denā as a compound giving verb. These affirmative imperative responses consist of de “give” plus the give auxiliary, inflected as de/do, so the same lexical family occurs twice in distinct ordered positions. CDIAL 6141 explains the de stem through MIA dēti and the imperative dēhi. The second occurrence is retained rather than deduplicated; mixed imperative/past responses are excluded from this group.

proposals.evidence: The complete response is de “give” plus diyā/diyo “gave” as perfective auxiliary. Platts documents de-denā; CDIAL 6141 supplies the first member and specifically 6140,3 *dita gives the second, including the contracted dyo form. Both components are represented in order; this is not an undivided descendant of either Sanskrit head.

proposals.evidence: The complete imperative response is ā “come” plus jā/jo “go” as auxiliary. Platts explicitly records ā-jānā; Turner places the regional ā/āv come stem under āpayati 1200 and jā under yāti 10452. Both ordered component families are represented. This follows Turner’s come-stem analysis rather than silently substituting the different āgata perfect stem or āgacchati family.
